A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same strategic-classification framework. Their main text, equations, proofs, appendices, and v2's experimental figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical results, proofs, and motivating examples, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes, including in its appendices.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original synthetic classification experiments, with training and validation loss curves, baseline comparisons, and confidence intervals.

M1.justification: Appendix A introduces a limited variant of the agent model: utility calculations use biased estimates of other agents' true features. The main linear classifier, potential maximization, and equilibrium-gradient training approach are retained.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates no datasets. v2 introduces training and validation on scikit-learn-generated, two-class synthetic datasets in Section 6 and Appendix D, establishing the paper's first empirical task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds two evaluated comparators where v1 had none: a classifier trained on truthful reports in Figure 1, and a cost-only strategic-training baseline in Figure 2. The latter mimics the classical setting of Hardt et al. (2016) and is evaluated under externalities.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an experimental protocol that samples groups, computes their PNE during training and validation, and tracks BCE loss over approximately 40 epochs. Figures 1–2 use k = 8, 10, 12 and (alpha, beta) = (0.1, 0.5), (0.2, 1.0), (0.3, 1.5). v1 has no corresponding experiments.

E4.justification: The new experiments test sensitivity to agent count and jointly increased cost/externality strength across nine configurations. Appendix D additionally tests the consequence of excluding externalities during training. v1 contains no empirical ablations or sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Figures 1–2 introduce means over 15 random datasets and 90% confidence intervals. v1 contains no empirical repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds learning curves showing declining strategic training and validation losses and generally lower final validation loss than both baselines. It also reports different baseline trends with group size and penalty strength. These are new empirical findings; v1 has no corresponding measurements.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds Proposition 3 and its proof, bounding an agent's perceived deviation gain by 2λ||b_i|| under biased feature estimates. Existing principal results and proofs are retained, including relocated proofs of Theorems 3–4. v2 also removes v1's explicit positive-definite-Hessian qualification of strict convexity in Section 3.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and concluding summary retain the same central claims: modeling inter-agent externalities, obtaining a unique computable PNE under structural conditions, establishing PAC guarantees, and differentiating through equilibrium. The added experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds tentative explanations linking stronger penalties to reduced manipulation, larger groups to steadier externalities, and cost-only training to excessive anticipated manipulation. Its discussion also raises coalitions with transferable utility. The existing central limitations concerning structural assumptions and known costs/externalities remain.

D1.justification: Section 6 newly identifies scikit-learn for data generation and cvxpylayers for equilibrium computation and differentiation, and documents the experimental cost/externality expressions and normalization. Disclosure remains limited: dataset dimensions and sizes, split proportions, optimizer settings, and code access are not provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning limited information and fairness, imperfect-information strategic classification, and experimental tools, including Harris et al., Heidari et al., Jagadeesan et al., Xie and Zhang, Agrawal et al., and Pedregosa et al. The main positioning against independent-agent and graph-based strategic classification remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially restructures Section 4 by moving the full proofs of Theorems 3–4 into Appendix B while retaining statements and sketches in the main text. Appendices are organized as A–D, and experiments precede the discussion. Most retained prose is unchanged; author order and the equal-contribution note also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds two nine-panel figures with loss axes, parameter labels, colored curves, legends, and confidence bands to a previously figure-free paper. Figure 2 redisplays the strategic curves with the cost-only comparator. Paragraph spacing and page layout are also extensively reflowed.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1's theoretical treatment, v2 adds useful synthetic evidence for equilibrium-aware training through relevant baseline comparisons and uncertainty reporting, plus a limited imperfect-information bound. These gains are tempered by sparse experimental specifications and removal of the explicit Hessian qualification, which reduces mathematical precision. The main theoretical contribution remains essentially unchanged.
